# House-Ad Template Brief — The Branded Creative Frame (Trade Dress)

*Prepared for the owner and trademark counsel as part of the Trademarks packet. It explains the branded ad
template, why it is **trade dress** (not a simple design mark), what to claim, and the realistic path to
protection. **Not legal advice** — registrability and the filing are counsel's to determine, and trade dress in
particular is a fact-specific, higher-bar question. Current as of 2026-09-07.*

---

## 1. What the template is

The house-ad template is the consistent **branded "shell"** the platform stamps on **every ad and AI-generated
creative**, across all three advertiser tiers (`ad-branding.ts` / `BrandedAd.jsx`). It is made of a small set of
fixed brand elements arranged the same way every time:

- the **website-link bar** at the top ("getgoodsgratis.com"),
- the **"G³" watermark** behind the content,
- the **frame / overall layout**,

with the advertiser's own creative dropped into the middle. Whatever product a given ad promotes, the *frame*
makes it recognizable as coming from Get Goods Gratis. That consistent overall look is the thing this brief is
about.

## 3. Why this is *trade dress*, not a simple design mark

The logo, the slogan, and the watermark are ordinary marks — a design mark, a word mark, and the same design
mark again. The **template is different**: you're not protecting a single graphic, you're protecting the
**overall look and arrangement** applied across many different creatives. That is **trade dress**. Trade dress is
protectable, but it must clear two bars the other marks don't:

- **Distinctiveness.** The look must identify *you* as the source. It is either **inherently distinctive** or it
  has acquired **secondary meaning** — i.e., consumers have come to associate that frame with your brand through
  use over time. A brand-new template usually leans on the *acquired* route, which takes time and evidence.
- **Non-functionality.** You cannot protect features that are functional (there for utility, not branding). The
  **placeholder creative area** is functional space and is *not* claimed; what you claim are the **branded
  elements** — the website-link bar, the "G³" watermark, and their arrangement/frame.

## 4. What to claim vs. exclude (for counsel)

- **Claim:** the website-link bar, the "G³" watermark, and the consistent frame/arrangement — the elements that
  signal source.
- **Exclude:** the advertiser-creative placeholder area (functional), and the AI-generated disclosure label
  (regulatory). The drawing above already excludes the disclosure label for this reason.
- Counsel should decide whether to pursue this on the **Principal Register** (needs inherent or acquired
  distinctiveness) or hold it until secondary meaning is demonstrable.

## 5. Why it's worth pursuing

It's the one asset that protects the *look of your entire ad output* without registering each image. The AI
pipeline produces an open-ended stream of per-advertiser creatives — those aren't your marks and can't be
registered — but the **frame stamped on all of them** can be, and protecting it stops a competitor from copying
your recognizable ad presentation. It also builds on, and reinforces, the logo and watermark filings.

## 6. Filing considerations

- **Type:** trade dress / design mark (special form drawing above).
- **Class:** 35 (advertising / marketing services) is the natural home; counsel confirms.
- **Basis:** Intent-to-Use (1(b)) or Use (1(a)); **specimen** = real served ads showing the frame in commerce
  (the platform already stamps it, so specimens are easy to produce).
- **Distinctiveness evidence** (if the acquired route is needed): volume/duration of use, examples across
  advertisers, any recognition data — worth starting to keep now.

## 7. Honest priority note

Trade dress is a **higher bar and a slower road** than the word and design marks. **File the core marks first**
— the **"Get Goods Gratis" word mark, the "G³" logo, and the slogan** — and treat the template as a **secondary,
"counsel-to-assess" filing** that may need acquired distinctiveness to land. Do **not** hold up the core filings
waiting on it. Keeping the template in consistent use now is exactly what builds the secondary meaning it will
likely need later.
